text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- The regional Freedom Party in Carinthia said public construction contracts should only go to firms that do not employ foreigners
- After Burgenland, Carinthia has the lowest number of foreign building workers at just over 1,000
- Foreign guest workers get the worst jobs and are generally poorly paid.
- Flixible working hours: back to the future. While the social partners struggled to find an agreement, the daily reality of business overtook them.
- Slight improvement in unemployment levels. In mid-February the number of jobless had fallen back below 300,000.
- Chrysler is scrapping a planned third shift at its Graz plant for production of the Voyager minivan.
- The post will introduce new telephone charges from mid-1997. Long distance calls should be significantly cheaper but local calls may be more expensive.
- The textile sector will cut 6.2 percent of jobs this year as it restructures.
- The Supreme Court has overruled a health ministry decision banning the planting in the open of genetically manipulated potatos.
- European Commission Mario Monti signed the wrong letter to Austria. The Commission has yet to send the right letter, telling Austria it has two months to outlaw anonymous savings accounts.
- Moody's cuts First Austrian bank's financial strength rating to C+ from B, following the bank's failure to win a stake in Creditanstalt.
- The biggest hurdle to the Post Office's planned listing on the Vienna stock exchange by the end of 1999 will be payments related to staff reduction.
- The Vienna bourse faces a mass exodus of firms if it does not tighten controls and do something to stimulate trade.
